<a id="body"></a>

## Body

Adding a field for persistence to a shared serde descriptor can also expose it through raw APIs, durable events and generic human CLI printers. Reviewing only a dedicated status/cache formatter does not prove "never shown."

In #265 at `9e665af8b04ef4fc03f309cfa8fb7d02211e3386`, cache-route `anchor` has trusted local registration provenance, but `SeatDescriptor` serialization carries it into roster/identity/directory responses and `seat.put` events. Generic response/event printers can show it even though dedicated cache/list lines and ping/doctor cache-seat lists omit it. The PID/start tuple was not an established credential disclosure; keep the visibility requirement discrepancy separate from exploit grading under C33.

Evidence: `crates/store/src/registry.rs:342`, `crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:996,4147`, `crates/daemon/src/community/directory.rs:464`, `crates/cli/src/main.rs:1544-1587`, `crates/cli/src/lib.rs:50-97`.

Also distinguish local authority from federated display: a remote peer's roster may deserialize the field without gaining a write to the local registration registry (`crates/daemon/src/federation/fanin.rs:245-287`).

Magic wand: a projection contract test that names permitted storage/event/API/human visibility, so an internal-field claim is checked rather than inferred from one formatter.
